string.text: {=ad1259vlach_culture_description}The Vlachs are a Romance-speaking people of the Carpathians and the lower Danube, heirs of the Latin-speaking provincials of Roman Dacia and Moesia. In the mid-thirteenth century their kenezates and voivodeships in Oltenia, Muntenia and the lands beyond the Siret owe allegiance to the crowns of Bulgaria and Hungary, yet keep their own law, their own boyars and the Orthodox faith. Shepherds drive their flocks between mountain pastures and the Danube plain, villages cluster in the shelter of the great forests, and Vlach warriors are known for ambushes in wooded passes and for light horsemen who ride alongside the Cumans.
{=ad1259vlach_vassal_intro}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK} of the house of {CLAN_NAME}, my {?PLAYER.GENDER}lady{?}lord{\?}, and I am honored to serve you.
{=ad1259vlach_noble_intro_clan}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the {CLAN_NAME}. My forefathers held these valleys before any king north or south of the Danube.
{=ad1259vlach_noble_intro_honor}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the house of {CLAN_NAME}, one of the old boyar lineages of the Vlachs.

{=ad1259vlach_noble_intro_mercy}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the house of {CLAN_NAME}. A boyar is only as good as the shepherds and ploughmen who look to him, and we have never forgotten it.
{=ad1259vlach_noble_intro_boasting}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the house of {CLAN_NAME}. From the Iron Gates to the Siret, every shepherd sings of our deeds.
{=ad1259vlach_noble_intro_cruel}I am {CONVERSATION_CHARACTER.LINK}, of the house of {CLAN_NAME}. Ask the Tatars who came through our passes how the house of {CLAN_NAME} greets its guests.
